evidence_levels.semantics: Ordered weakest to strongest. evidence_level is the highest level the gate's artefacts substantiate and can never exceed evidence_level_ceiling, which is the most the gate's own command can ever support; a lower level must never stand in for a higher one. Gates with no captured log substantiate nothing and report the vocabulary floor. A level only counts as substantiated evidence when the record's status is PASS; FAIL, NOT_RUN and unknown records keep the level for context but must never be aggregated as evidence at that level.

status_semantics.PASS: The gate's own exit status is 0.
status_semantics.FAIL: The gate failed with a non-zero exit status.
status_semantics.NOT_RUN: No log and no result file exist; the gate was not run for this candidate.
status_semantics.unknown: Evidence exists but the exit status could not be derived or a result file was stale/unprovable; never read as success.

determinism: This index contains no generation timestamp: per-gate timing comes only from captured start markers and log modification times, so repeated runs over unchanged artefacts are byte-identical.
methodology: Every field is derived from artefacts on disk: a result file supplies an exit status only when its gate id, command, source commit, candidate digest, log SHA-256 and declared-artifact SHA-256 bind to the current index context; otherwise stale or unprovable result files are ignored and a PASS marker is never inferred from that log. Without a trusted result file, exit status comes from a decisive terminal log marker, timing from a captured start marker plus the log mtime, digests from SHA-256 of the log and of a declared artifact, and test counts from the log when the format is known. Any value that could not be derived is the explicit string 'unknown' and any gate without a log is reported as NOT_RUN; no gate is ever omitted and no measurement, host, timestamp or customer fact is invented.
